observable_outcome: A Requirement carries the instant it was captured, taken once from the transaction's authority time so it is byte-identical to its own requirement.captured event and stable across a transaction retry, persisted by both store adapters, and reported through the Requirement read models -- omitted entirely for a record captured before the field existed rather than reported as the zero instant. The ordering rule that prevents starvation therefore has a genuinely varying input, and the interval of capture-time spread within which V2-030's starvation bound is a true statement is derived from the declared weights, asserted at both endpoints, and recorded together with the fact that nothing in production bounds that spread. No scheduler decision rule, weight or bound changes, and no existing scheduler test is edited.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written before any code. The evidence opens with a table stating, one row each: what this task records (a capture time on the Requirement), what it exposes (the read models and the openapi response schemas), what it proves about V2-030's bound and the exact interval within which that bound holds, what it declares but does not apply (the legacy mapping rule, applied by V2-068), and what it deliberately does not do (no decision rule, weight or bound change; no Snapshot builder; no export-record change). A further row must state that no production code constructs a scheduler.Snapshot at this commit, with the argv that establishes it. Nothing in the evidence may claim that the scheduler is wired to the running system, and nothing may claim any release gate.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything. Record top-level test names and counts and that all pass for internal/domain (37 at the starting commit), internal/scheduler (20), internal/application (49), internal/api (20), internal/store/memory (4) and internal/store/firestore (9). Record the measured facts this task acts on: domain.Requirement's complete field list is ID, Status, Version, Increments, StableSnapshot, RequestedBy and none of them carries a json tag; internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:59 declares CreatedAt on the scheduler's own Requirement; internal/scheduler/source_guard_test.go pins a single-entry non-standard-library import allowlist; a search for internal/scheduler across every *.go outside the package returns exactly two hits, both assertion-data string literals in internal/ci; and starvation_test.go's own comments state three times that every candidate shares one CreatedAt so the age term cancels. Every pre-existing test must still pass at the end under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged, and before/after top-level counts per touched package must be reported.

A3. The domain edit and its closure. domain.Requirement gains exactly one field, CapturedAt time.Time, with no json tag, plus one predicate CaptureRecorded() bool returning whether it is non-zero. Assert: Validate accepts both a zero and a non-zero value for every valid Requirement status; every RequirementCommandKind through DecideRequirement leaves CapturedAt byte-identical, asserted by a table over every command kind rather than a sample; CompleteRequirementFromRelease leaves it byte-identical; and no new import appears in any file in internal/domain. Assert by git diff that the only file changed under internal/domain is model.go plus the new and existing test files named in allowed_paths, and that internal/domain/source_guard_test.go is not edited and all four of its tests still pass under their own names.

A4. The value comes from the transaction authority time, once. Capture sets CapturedAt from the authority time already carried by the transaction context -- the same accessor Service.record uses at internal/application/service.go:1386-1393 -- and not from a second s.clock.Now() call. Assert: the stored CapturedAt equals the At of the requirement.captured event recorded by the same operation, compared value to value; CaptureRequest gains no field and a request body carrying a captured_at field is rejected with 400; the value is stable across a Firestore transaction retry, driven through the adapter's retry path, or recorded as skipped with its reason if that path cannot be driven; and a clock returning zero still produces the existing error rather than a zero capture time.

A5. Neither read time nor event scan may substitute for it. Assert: reading the same Requirement at two different injected clock values produces byte-identical capture times; the capture time still reports correctly after the event log is emptied, proving no derivation from events; and an AST scan over the new read helper shows its only source is the Requirement record, with the matcher verified first against a known-positive and a known-negative. Assert there is no code path anywhere in the task's diff that assigns CapturedAt from a clock read outside Capture.

A6. Legacy records. A Requirement with a zero CapturedAt is valid, and the read view omits captured_at entirely rather than emitting 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z. Assert: Validate accepts it; RequirementDetailView and RequirementView omit the key from the marshalled JSON, checked by scanning the marshalled bytes for the key and for the literal 0001-01-01; capturedAtView returns nil for a legacy record and a copy (not a pointer into stored state) for a recorded one, asserted by mutating through the returned pointer and re-reading; and a store round-trip of a document written without the field yields a legacy record rather than an error, exercised on both adapters.

A7. The mapping rule for a missing capture time, declared and proven. Assert in internal/scheduler that a candidate presented with a CreatedAt equal to the snapshot's Now (age zero) is ordered below an otherwise identical candidate with a real earlier capture time, and that a candidate presented with a zero CreatedAt would instead outrank every other candidate regardless of priority -- run the second case explicitly as a positive control and record the computed scores, so the evidence shows why the rule is age zero and not the zero instant. State the rule in the documentation in one sentence: a Requirement with no recorded capture time is ordered as if captured at the snapshot's Now, never as an unbounded age.

A8. The capture-time spread interval, derived then measured. In a new file internal/scheduler/capture_time_test.go, parameterize D -- the number of seconds by which the flood candidates' capture time precedes the waiter's -- and assert, with the derivation written in a comment from the declared numbers only (flood 30000 + age, waiter 23500 + 2500*(tick-1) + age, strict greater-than because flood ids sort before 'important' under the comparator at scheduler.go:154-157, StarvationBoundTicks = 5): (a) convergence within StarvationBoundTicks at D = -6500, D = -1, D = 0, D = 999, D = 1000 and D = 3499, recording the tick each converges on; (b) as a positive control, that at D = 3500 the waiter is NOT assigned within StarvationBoundTicks, with the tick it would converge on recorded; (c) as a positive control, that at D = -6501 the negative control (StarvationRisk term neutralised the same way starvation_test.go does it, restored via defer) DOES converge, so the proof stops attributing convergence to that term; (d) that the one-tick margin V2-030 recorded exists only for D below 1000, recorded as a measured statement. Declare the interval as a documented constant with the derivation. Do not edit starvation_test.go, starvationScenario, priority.go, decision.go, scheduler.go or any weight, and do not change StarvationBoundTicks.

A9. Escalation, recorded not fixed. Record in the evidence and in the documentation that nothing in production bounds D, that a flood whose candidates were captured more than 3499 seconds before the waiter can exceed the declared bound, and that every available remedy -- raising the StarvationRisk step, normalizing or capping the age term, raising StarvationBoundTicks -- is a decision-rule change forbidden to this task by non_goal 3. Name the owner of the follow-up decision and stop there. Do not weaken, relax or reword any existing assertion to make the limit disappear.

A10. Persistence in both stores, one behavioural table. Assert on both internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore, using the same test table: a captured Requirement round-trips its capture time unchanged; a rolled-back transaction leaks no capture time into committed state; a document written before the field existed reads back as a legacy record; and the value is unchanged by every lifecycle transition applied through the service. Do not edit internal/store/memory/store.go or internal/store/firestore/store.go: if either adapter needs a production change to carry the field, stop and escalate, because the design's claim is that plain json.Marshal and state.clone() already carry it.

A11. Read and API surface. RequirementDetailView and RequirementView gain captured_at as an optional pointer; add the field to the corresponding response schemas in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, which set additionalProperties:false so the addition is required. Assert every existing openapi-conformance assertion in internal/contracts and internal/release still passes, that the response carries no field this Work Order did not name, and that GET /v1/requirements and GET /v1/requirements/{id} keep their existing status codes and role gating. The export record is NOT changed: assert that the marshalled ExportRequirement shape is byte-identical to the baseline for the same input, so no export digest moves.

A12. Owner console. Append one self-contained block to internal/web/owner.html and one to internal/web/owner.js, each introduced by a comment naming V2-073, at the end of the file, changing no existing byte. The block must show a Requirement's capture time when recorded and show plainly that it is absent when the record is legacy -- not an empty string, and not the zero instant. Add no external asset, script or font. Assert the rendered markup contains no credential-shaped and no email-shaped value.

A13. Documentation. Extend docs/operations/scheduler-local.md with a section recording: that the Requirement now carries a capture time and where it comes from; the legacy omission and the mapping rule from A7; the derived capture-time spread interval from A8 with its arithmetic; the escalation from A9; and that the Snapshot builder does not exist yet and V2-068 owns wiring the value into it. Do not edit any other document and do not edit docs/operations/self-update.md.

A14. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test; every wait is a bounded deadline poll over an injected clock and every timestamp comes from an injected clock, including every capture time in every fixture. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/domain ./internal/scheduler ./internal/application ./internal/api three times in sequence and record that the verdict line and the output are identical each time, and run it once with -race.

A15. Measured notes for V2-045, recorded and not acted on. Record that this task creates no new import edge -- internal/domain gains no import, the new internal/scheduler test imports only internal/domain which the package already imports, and application, api and both stores already declare their dependencies -- and that it moves the domain, application, scheduler, api, store-memory, store-firestore, web, contracts and docs component keys, the domain key being the DAG root so the fan-out is wide. Record that editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts key, a declared contract dependency of the api and control-plane components. Only the domain, scheduler and application evidence records are issued here; name V2-045 as the owner of the remaining key movement under gate rule G6. V2-045 has landed, so internal/ci's manifest check will turn make check red if the declared component dependencies and the real import graph diverge: because this design creates no edge, a red manifest or dependency-coverage check means the design was departed from -- stop and escalate to the tech_lead and do not edit ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*.

A16. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-073-domain.json (id ev-v2-073-domain, component domain), .agents/v2/evidence/V2-073-scheduler.json (id ev-v2-073-scheduler, component scheduler) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-073-application.json (id ev-v2-073-application, component application), each with task_id V2-073 and correlation_id v2-073-requirement-capture-time, recording for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, with every acceptance item traceable to a named check. The scheduler record must carry the full A8 table: D, the tick of convergence, and the pass or fail verdict for each value. Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). A skipped test is recorded with status skipped and never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Register all three with exactly three appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the records in place. Any digest written in prose must match the .gitleaks.toml allowlist shape (64 or 40 hex characters, at most one trailing punctuation character).

A17. Component evidence keys. The evidence_key recorded in each artifact is that component's key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added: a new file that is not yet in the index is invisible to the git ls-files based input set that key is derived from.

A18. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs and judge them by the verdict line, not by the shell exit status. No file outside allowed_paths changes.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

internal/domain/model.go is the only production file under internal/domain that may change, and the only permitted change is one field on Requirement plus one predicate. Do not add an import, do not add a Validate clause that can reject a zero value, do not touch any transition function's assignments, and do not edit internal/domain/source_guard_test.go or internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go.

Do not change any scheduler decision rule, weight, clamp, comparator or bound. priority.go, decision.go and scheduler.go are read-only, StarvationBoundTicks is unchanged, and starvation_test.go, priority_test.go, scheduler_test.go, rollback_test.go and budget_test.go are not edited.
Do not make the capture-time spread limit disappear by weakening, relaxing or rewording an assertion. The limit is the finding; record it and escalate the remedy.
Do not derive the capture time from a read time, from a scan of events, or from any clock read outside Capture. It is set once, at intake, from the transaction authority time.
Do not emit the zero instant for a legacy record. The read view omits the field entirely, and no consumer may be handed 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z.

Do not build a scheduler.Snapshot or a mapper from application types to scheduler types. No production code constructs a Snapshot at this commit and V2-068 owns the builder; a mapper in internal/application would create an application-to-scheduler import edge that only V2-045 may declare.

Do not edit internal/store/memory/store.go or internal/store/firestore/store.go. If either adapter needs a production change to persist the field, stop and escalate: the design's claim is that the existing plain json.Marshal and state.clone() already carry it.
Do not change the export record or any export digest. Assert the marshalled ExportRequirement shape is byte-identical to the baseline.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. This design creates no new import edge, so a red manifest or dependency-coverage check in make check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than editing any of those files.
Do not edit contracts/release-contract/** and do not weaken any capability declaration there.
Do not edit .agents/v2/task-state/**, any .agents/v2/packets/** file, or .agents/v2/provider-preflight/**.
Do not edit docs/operations/self-update.md or any document other than docs/operations/scheduler-local.md.
Both owner console files are effectively single-line minified documents: append a self-contained block introduced by a comment naming V2-073 at the end of each, and change no existing byte.

Do not start a real Provider CLI and do not touch any Google Cloud resource. The Firestore assertions run through the local emulator path scripts/firestore-emulator.sh already provides for make component-store-firestore.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Every capture time in every fixture comes from an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip with status skipped and its reason, and record the execution environment identifier.
Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.
Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged. Report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.
